mappedContracts.statement: Create a canonical machine-readable implementation contract derived from this prompt and make it the binding source of truth for all subsequent work.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract records this prompt's SHA-256, every contract ID, phase, track, task, dependency decision, acceptance criterion, GitHub issue reference, Conductor path, status, evidence, and exception.
A deterministic validator fails on missing mappings, duplicate IDs, invalid states, orphaned tasks, unapproved scope changes, or completion without evidence.
Every implementation PR runs the contract validator as a required check.

mappedContracts.statement: Use the newest supported Node.js Current release and newest compatible npm release as the main development, CI, build, test, and release baseline.
acceptanceCriteria: Pin the exact runtime in packageManager/devEngines and standard toolchain files.
Remove Node 18 and Node 20 support claims.
Required CI runs on the current runtime across Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Use relevant current-runtime experimental capabilities, including the permission model and configuration features, under the normal required test suite.

mappedContracts.statement: Replace misleading headline coverage with risk-weighted assurance and remove blanket exclusions from high-risk modules.
acceptanceCriteria: Credential, authorization, policy, planning, mutation, state, media, billing, subscriber, team, and MCP HTTP code has explicit branch and mutation targets.

mappedContracts.statement: Provide one deterministic verification command that runs contracts, generation drift, types, lint, tests, coverage, mutation, fuzz smoke, package checks, MCP conformance, security checks, and receipt generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The command works locally and in CI.
It emits a machine-readable verification receipt conforming to repository-standards.
Release consumes the same verified artefacts rather than rebuilding differently.

mappedContracts.statement: Run blocking checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows using the main Node Current runtime and exact package-manager version.
acceptanceCriteria: Path, permissions, shell, browser-profile, atomic-state, package-install, and completion behaviour are tested across platforms.
OneDrive/SharePoint scenarios receive dedicated Windows tests.
No obsolete Node support lane remains.
